spec_match.rationale: Exercises the SVG2 text-on-path layout rules the side attribute plugs into: open-path glyph hiding (mid < 0 or > length), closed-subpath wrapping with text-anchor, and side reversing before offsets apply — each paired with getExtentOfChar-measured counts.

interactive.rationale: Path select (open vs Z-closed), side radios, a -25%..125% startOffset slider, and a text-anchor select all re-measure and re-render live, including a real all-glyphs-hidden state.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises edge behaviour with measured glyph counts; the page measures visible counts, index ranges, and positions after every change.

edge_cases.rationale: This IS the edge-case page: off-both-ends clipping, negative offsets, closed-path wrap, anchor interaction; the closed-path copy explicitly notes browsers differ and defers to the measured numbers instead of asserting spec-perfect wrapping.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5422782593761280 and the spec's TextLayoutPath rules section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the passing-today startOffset geometry (startoffset-moves-first-glyph) and the side geometry this page reports on; the wrap behaviour is deliberately reported, not asserted, because the spec leaves browsers measurably divergent.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified headless (Chromium 141): slider driven to 125% measured 0 visible glyphs, path switch re-measured length (352.4px open curve to 565.6px closed loop), console clean; screenshots read at both device classes.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts glyph-visibility-measured once on load plus the supported/fallback side probe asserts; per-interaction logging is single-line and intentional.

design_system.rationale: Path, start dot, and text are variable-driven classes; the measurement table reuses the shared stone/paper/black pairs, all AA.

accessibility.rationale: Native select/radio/slider controls with labels and legends, svg role=img with desc, visible focus, and a single debounced polite readout announcing the measured visibility summary.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Controls flex-wrap, the table sits in its own overflow-x scroller, the SVG scales via viewBox; no horizontal page overflow at 360px; verified at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800.

openQuestions.title: Measure closed-path wrapping against the spec matrix on Chrome 156
openQuestions.detail: SVG2's closed-subpath visibility windows depend on (text-anchor, direction) pairs. On a supporting build, walk the anchor select on the closed loop at several offsets with side left and right, record the measured visible ranges, and consider promoting any behaviour Chrome implements faithfully into new additive conformance assertions.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce live state changes screen reader aria-live
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Debounce frequently-changing live regions so slider scrubbing does not spam announcements; keep the region polite and singular.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The startOffset slider fires on input but the readout announcement is debounced at 300ms into one polite output; the measurement table updates silently for sighted scanning.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wrap control rows with flex-wrap, give tables an explicit overflow-x auto container rather than letting them widen the page.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Controls use flex-wrap with logical min() widths, and the measurement table is inside a dedicated .scroller with overflow-x: auto — the page body itself never scrolls horizontally.

summary: The edge/failure angle: open-path clipping, closed-path wrapping, startOffset from -25% to 125%, and text-anchor interaction, all reported as measured glyph counts and positions. side="right" rows are honestly labelled as no-ops on the unsupported Chromium 141 build environment, while the clipping behaviour is fully exercisable there today.
